I'm spotting the real bug: the lookup does an exact, case-sensitive match against the order ID, so when the customer types "a-1001" lowercase instead of "A-1001", it fails to find the record and reports "not found" even though the order exists.

I should be able to test lookupOrder directly without needing the model or API key — I'll try running it via tsx with both 'a-1001' and 'A-1001' to confirm the case-sensitivity theory before patching.

The order keys are plain ASCII, so the data is fine. The suspect is the lookup: `ORDERS[orderId]` is case-sensitive and does no trimming, so `a-1001` would miss `A-1001`. I'll confirm by calling the tool directly with a few input variants.

text: The tsc output being empty confirms there are no type errors, so that check passes. Now I'll move on to writing the answer.json file.
The fix works for all variants and unknown ids still return `null`. Now I'll write `answer.json`.

The root cause is in `lookupOrder` (`src/tools.ts`): it did an exact, case-sensitive lookup on the raw order id, so `a-1001` or an id with stray whitespace returned `null`, and the agent reported the order as not found. I changed the lookup to `ORDERS[orderId.trim().toUpperCase()] ?? null`. Calling the tool directly now returns the shipped record for `a-1001`, `" A-1001 "` and `"A-1001\n"`, and an unknown id still returns `null`. The project type-checks cleanly.

`answer.json` is written in the project root. I did not run the Genkit flow itself, since it needs a model call; the check was on the tool directly. I also didn't touch `createRefund` in `src/db.ts`, which has the same exact-match lookup, so a refund request with a lowercase id would still fail.
